headline: Equities and bonds are more correlated than usual, reducing diversification benefits; most asset classes share the same underlying drivers (inflation, rates, economic environment)
reasoning: Angela Ashton notes that equities and bonds are currently more correlated than they have been for some time. She observes that most investable asset classes share the same fundamental return drivers — inflation, interest rates, and the general economic environment — meaning that even a seemingly diversified portfolio of 10-15 asset classes may not provide genuine diversification. She emphasises that negative correlation is not required to gain diversification benefit; lowering overall correlation is sufficient.
quote: The problem is that most asset classes that we can invest in are pretty like have some correlation to equities and bonds. And the the reason for that is that the underlying drivers for most asset class returns are actually very similar and most of them are sort of around inflation, interest rates, general economic environment and so forth. So the problem is that we've got, you know, you, you might think you've got 10 asset classes or 15 asset classes, but in reality they're all being driven by the same sorts of things.
